newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK political concerns toughen expats' life - study.
newsitem.headline: HK political concerns toughen expats' life - study.

text.p: The prospect of political tension ahead of Hong Kong's 1997 return to China is making life tougher for expatriates in the British colony, a study showed on Sunday.

ECA International's 1996 ranking analysis downgraded the territory's rating on living conditions for Westerners to B/C from last year's A/B in the biggest demotion of the 160 countries surveyed, the Hong Kong Standard newspaper said.

"The prospect of political tensions and culture clashes with China, coupled with increasing threats to personal security, contributed to Hong Kong's rating as a destination for expatriate employees as 1997 approaches," the survey was quoted as saying.
Hong Kong reverts to China next July 1, after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
The study, with a rating scale from A to F, gauged key aspects of expatriate lifestyles, including quality of health care and education facilities, political tensions and personal security.
China ranked E. Its rating was kept down by personal security threats and high pollution levels, the newspaper said.
